text: In Flask, you define routes using the `@app.route()` decorator. By default, routes only accept GET requests. To accept other methods, use `@app.route('/items', methods=['POST'])`.
To read JSON data sent in a POST or PUT request, use `request.json` from the `flask` module.
To return JSON responses, you can use Flask's `jsonify()` function. For example: `return jsonify({"message": "Success"}), 201`.
Use a global Python dictionary (e.g., `registry = {}`) to store the items in-memory. Use a counter variable to generate unique IDs for new items.
